translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation loses the specific grammatical gender agreement of the verb 'dhoondhta hoon' (masculine speaker) which is flattened into the gender-neutral English 'I search'.

The translation of 'soch ke perton mein' as 'layers of thought' loses the grammatical feminine gender of 'soch' (thought) and the specific plural postpositional phrasing 'ke perton' (in the layers of).

metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting a literal second person sleeping peacefully next to the awake speaker might look like a simple domestic scene rather than a poetic personification of sleep itself.
metaphor_spans.tenor: The state of sleep being completely unavailable and distant from the speaker
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Show a faint, anthropomorphic figure made of soft starlight or mist curled up asleep on a distant cloud or roof, visible to the viewer but out of reach of the awake speaker.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation 'It must be sleeping somewhere' for 'kahin vo kahin soya hai' loses the double use of 'kahin' (somewhere) which creates a rhythmic, hesitant poetic cadence in Hindi.

The translation loses the personification nuance of sleep ('vo... soya hai') being grammatically masculine here, matching the masculine noun 'tukda' (piece) of sleep, which is rendered as a neutral 'it' in English.

original_poem:
मैं ढूंढता हूँ रात में
नींद का एक टुकड़ा,
कभी छत पर, कभी बिस्तर में,
कभी सोच के परतों में।

वो जो कहीं खो गया है
मुझे उसी की तलाश है,
रातों के अंधेरों में
कहीं वो कहीं सोया है।

कभी तकिये के नीचे,
कभी तकिये से परे,
एक टुकड़ा नींद का,
जो शायद मेरा था, कहीं गिर गया है।
translated_poem:
I search in the night
For a piece of sleep,
Sometimes on the roof, sometimes in bed,
Sometimes in layers of thought.

That which is lost somewhere,
Is what I seek,
In the darkness of the night
It must be sleeping somewhere.

Sometimes under the pillow,
Sometimes beyond it,
A piece of sleep,
That perhaps was mine, has fallen somewhere.
